18.description: The committee recommends City Council approve a $121,750 bonus payment to SREDA and its 2026 performance targets. SREDA is launching a new Concierge program for businesses.

chips.text: Businesses in mining, manufacturing, agriculture, and life sciences are targeted.
SREDA's new Concierge program for businesses will launch in May.

19.description: The committee recommends approving tax abatements for six businesses that invested $25.7 million and created 90 new jobs, aiming to boost Saskatoon's economy.

chips.text: Four future companies are expected to invest $142 million and create over 200 jobs.

20.description: The committee recommends City Council approve a $3,794,000 loan to purchase 3815 Wanuskewin Road and 3802 Arthur Rose Avenue for future city operations.

23.description: The committee recommends allocating $3.57 million from a reserve to acquire a four-acre parcel at 1080 Kensington Boulevard for a new Conseil des écoles fransaskoises school, and approving a lease.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer raised concerns about provincial 'surprises costing millions of dollars'.
New school will accommodate 400 students and provide 90 child care spaces.
This is the first CF school since the changes to the planning and development act.
Details of the province's cost-sharing formula for school land are still unknown.
Province committed to more robust long-term planning for school sites.

25.description: The city will negotiate and enter into license agreements for tenants at Gather Local Market and Ideas Inc. at 414 Avenue B South and 120 Sonnenschein Way, aiming for operational self-sufficiency.

chips.text: Councillor Dubois questioned if community benefits could lead to subsidized rents.
Staff explained balancing cost recovery with community benefit criteria.
Will community benefit criteria lead to city costs?

26.description: The committee recommends increasing budgets for several capital projects, including park upgrades, waste reduction, and water/sewer capacity, using over $11 million in government funding.

chips.text: Users of Ernest Lindor Park and city golf courses will see upgrades.
Funding will support waste reduction, tree planting, and energy efficiency.

27.description: The committee recommends updating several financial bylaws, including increasing the City Manager's authority to approve leases from $20,000 to $40,000, and repealing five fully repaid borrowing bylaws.

chips.text: First report in a series to review bylaws for new City's Act publication.

28.description: The committee recommends City Council reallocate $580,000 in federal Natural Infrastructure Fund money across nine capital projects to ensure full utilization of the funding.

chips.text: Funding supports creating and enhancing natural infrastructure.

29.description: The committee recommends a five-year property tax exemption for Saskatoon Soccer Inc. for the Kinsmen/Henk Ruys and Saskatoon Soccer Centres, from 2026 to 2030.

chips.text: Saskatoon Soccer Inc. is a non-profit corporation.

30.description: The city will renew seven farmland leases on city-owned agricultural lands for 2026. These leases, covering 359 to 622 acres each, generate revenue for the city.

chips.text: Farmers leasing city-owned agricultural lands will have their agreements renewed.

31.description: Saskatoon approved the demolition of former Transit buildings at 301-24th Street West, preparing the land for sale and redevelopment, with proceeds funding the South Caswell Hill Land Development project.

9.description: The committee recommends City Council be informed on two matters, without making any decisions or taking action.

24.description: Saskatoon's investment portfolio generated $27.9 million in 2025, contributing $19.4 million to the operating budget. Council also requested a forecast of investment variances for the fall budget.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer noted significant investment variances
Taxpayers benefit from $19.4 million contributed to the general operating budget.

22.description: The Board of Revision's 2025 annual report details handling nearly 1500 property assessment appeals, adjusting $452 million in property values. This informs council about the board's independent work.

chips.text: Councilors questioned inconsistent agenda placement for city-appointed board reports.
Property owners in every neighborhood appealed assessments totaling $7.2 billion.
Administration committed to reviewing consistency in scheduling annual board reports.
